subject: URGENT: Saffron Bios - hosted API latency spike after model-v3.2 canary
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@saffronbio.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: High p95/p99 after model-v3.2 canary (30%) - urgent

Dylan —

We started receiving alerts at ~07:50 PDT after you pushed model-v3.2 to canary at 30% traffic. Our latency SLO is 200ms p95; we're seeing p95 jump to ~980ms and p99 to ~2.3s. Error rates also crept up from 0.6% to ~3.8% and several downstream jobs are timing out which impacts inference-driven pipelines.

Attached are: trimmed access logs and a short trace dump (profiler_summary_0629.pdf). Can you confirm whether the canary is on the same kernel/quantization profile as previously? This is blocking a release on our end — we need a mitigation plan and ETA ASAP.

Jordan Lee
Platform Engineer, Saffron Bios
Attachments: saffron_logs_0629.zip, profiler_summary_0629.pdf
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@saffronbio.com>, support@saffronbio.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High p95/p99 after model-v3.2 canary (30%) - urgent

Thanks for the quick ping, Jordan — we see the same alerting in our monitoring. I'm looping in Monica (SRE) and Steph (PM) to investigate immediately.

Immediate plan:
- Monica: can you pull the profiler and route-level traces and confirm whether this regression correlates with model-v3.2 code paths (attention kernels / new kv-cache changes)?
- If confirmed, we will either roll back the canary to v3.1 or shift Saffron traffic to the stable cluster while we debug.

Jordan: we'll keep you updated every 15m until we stabilize. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is high impact.

— Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95/p99 after model-v3.2 canary (30%) - preliminary analysis

On Tue, Jun 29, 2026 at 08:32 AM PDT dylan.brooks@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks for the quick ping, Jordan — we see the same alerting in our monitoring. I'm looping in Monica (SRE) and Steph (PM) to investigate immediately.

Quick interim findings:
- Correlation: spike onset aligns with v3.2 canary rollout at 07:45 PDT.
- Metric delta: host-level CPU increased ~30%, GPU compute utilization shows more frequent small stalls, kv-cache hit-rate dropped ~14% on affected routes.
- Profiling: stack traces show higher time in fused attention kernel fallback paths for sequence lengths > 512 — looks like a kernel selection/quantization mismatch for v3.2 on our inference build.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Shift Saffron traffic to stable host pool (v3.1) — fastest (1-3m) and no code change.
2) Canary rollback of v3.2 globally (5-7m) — if other customers unaffected, heavier action.
3) Short-term autoscale bump for the affected pool + increased batching window (10-15m) — reduces p95 but raises cost.

I'm starting a scoped trace collection and attaching profiler_summary_0629.pdf to the incident. Dylan — please confirm which option Saffron prefers. Marcus, if we shift traffic, please prepare the routing change and confirm capacity.

Monica
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: p95-p99-traces-0629.txt
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@saffronbio.com>, support@saffronbio.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95/p99 after model-v3.2 canary (30%) - rollback initiated

Jordan —

We are moving Saffron traffic back to the v3.1 stable pool now (option 1). Marcus is executing the routing change; expected propagation ~2–4 minutes. We'll monitor p95/p99 and error-rate and follow up once we have stable numbers.

Next steps:
- If p95/p99 return to baseline within 10 minutes, we'll keep Saffron on v3.1 and wait until debugging is complete.
- Root cause postmortem to follow; we'll include kernel selection logs and quantization validation matrix.

Thanks for the patience — we'll send a status in 10m.

— Dylan
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@saffronbio.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: support@saffronbio.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95/p99 after model-v3.2 canary (30%) - rollback initiated

Dylan/Team —

Thanks for the fast action. We're already seeing p95 dropping toward normal (~150ms) and p99 trending down. Appreciate the rollback.

Two asks before we close the incident:
1) A short-term credit for the incident window (Saffron is a committed reserved capacity customer under DEAL-9843).
2) A plan/timeline for a fix that prevents future kernel-selection regressions during canaries — ideally a pre-deploy kernel compatibility test or a gated canary that checks p95/p99 on a synthetic replay before production traffic.

Jordan
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, leadership@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Saffron Bios incident - executive note and next steps

Team —

Thanks for the rapid containment. This is an executive-visible incident (Saffron is a strategic medical accounts customer). Please do the following ASAP:
- Confirm full restoration and send a concise incident summary to Saffron (what happened, rollback action, current metrics, immediate prevention).
- Approve a goodwill credit window (propose 6 hours of reserved capacity credit) and coordinate with finance for formal approval.
- Steph: schedule a postmortem with Engineering and SRE next week; include the model-onboarding and canary gate owners.
- Monica/Marcus: capture and preserve kernel/quantization traces and an anonymized artifact we can run in CI for future guardrails.

I'll loop in the CTO if needed but let's have the customer-facing note ready within the hour.

— Grace O'Connor
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
